prompt: The `curl` with the new account's token got a `Forbidden` answer naming `system:serviceaccount:shop:deployer`. Which step refused it?
hint: Did the API server know who was asking?

choices.text: Authentication: the token was not valid
choices.why: The message names the account, so the token was accepted.
Right. The identity was known; no rule granted it `list` on pods.

choices.text: TLS: `curl` did not trust the server
choices.why: A TLS failure would have stopped before any JSON came back.

choices.text: Admission, because the namespace was new
choices.why: Listing creates nothing, so admission never sees it.

prompt: Where is the user `kubernetes-admin` stored in the cluster?
hint: `kubectl auth whoami` showed where the name came from.

choices.why: Kubernetes has no User objects.
A ServiceAccount would appear as `system:serviceaccount:…`.
Right. People are names carried by certificates or tokens.

choices.text: In etcd, with a hashed password
choices.why: There is no password store for users.

prompt: The `deployer` account may `get` pods in `shop`. Why was `kubectl auth can-i create pods/exec` still `no`?

choices.why: No namespace has that rule.

choices.text: `pods/exec` is a subresource the Role never named
choices.why: Right. Each subresource is granted on its own, like `pods/log` was.

choices.text: ServiceAccounts may never exec into a pod
choices.why: A Role naming `pods/exec` with `create` would allow it.
`can-i` asks the authoriser; it never looks at a pod.

prompt: A RoleBinding in namespace `shop` binds a Role to `deployer`. What may `deployer` do in `default`?

choices.why: The answer for `default` was `no`.
Nothing grants reading there either.
Right. A RoleBinding grants inside its own namespace only.
No rules means refusal, not freedom.

prompt: A pod's token was issued for the pod `reader`. The pod is deleted, and a copy of the token is used a minute later. What happens?

choices.text: It works until `exp`, a year later
choices.why: The API server also checks that the pod still exists.

choices.text: It is refused, because the pod is gone
choices.why: Right. A bound token dies with the object it names.

choices.text: It works on the node it was issued for
choices.why: Nodes do not check API tokens.
Nothing downgrades a token.

prompt: A team should manage everything in namespace `team-a` and nothing elsewhere. Which grant does that?
hint: The reach comes from the binding.

choices.why: That grants `admin` in every namespace.

choices.text: A RoleBinding in `team-a` to the ClusterRole `admin`
choices.why: Right. A RoleBinding limits a ClusterRole to its own namespace.
That is everything, everywhere.
`view` reads; it does not manage.

prompt: A pod never talks to the API server. What should its spec say about the token?
hint: A token nobody uses can still be stolen.

choices.why: Right. Then there is no token in the container to steal.

choices.text: Nothing; unused tokens expire within the hour
choices.why: The mounted token was valid for a year.
That names an account called `none`, which does not exist.
It leaves the token mounted anyway.

prompt: Put in order what the API server does with a request from the pipeline.
items: Reads the token and decides who is asking
Looks for a binding that names that identity
Checks the bound role's rules for the verb and resource
trap: Nothing about permissions can be checked before the API server knows whose permissions to check.
